caption: Aaron "All Day" Lewis, previously a champion in TTW, the league UPW's own title lineage continues from, won UPW's own first post-relaunch World Heavyweight Championship and held it until Derek Rage dethroned him at Survival.

caption: Derek Rage battled through a rigged number-one contender's match to earn his shot at Aaron Lewis, then took the UPW World Heavyweight Championship from him at Survival and held it through the promotion's own final months.

name: Malcom Shabazz

tenures.finisher: Hard Truth (spinning flapjack into the turnbuckle)
tenures.note: Billed his own UPW run around claims of racist treatment by the promotion and its fans, backed by a stable of masked "Hard Truth Soldiers." Won a handicap match against the Brothers Grimm on 8 November 2016 to keep his job (with an assist from Liam Donegal counting his own pin using the knocked-out referee's arm), then fought a running program with Donegal that turned violent — a masked assault opening Donegal's manager Adam Lazarus's head, a televised threat against Donegal's wife and infant son. Arrested backstage on 18 February 2017 for a brawl that put UPW VP Thomas Grissom in the hospital, forfeiting a North American Title tournament match to Harrison Daniels III. Billed for an unheld 25 April 2017 card against "Top Dog" Rick Styles. "Malcom" is roster.html's own spelling; "Malcolm" appears at least once in the served show text (The Hype's popsicle-naming bit) and is carried as an aka rather than corrected.

caption: Malcom Shabazz built his UPW run around a racism storyline against the promotion itself, feuding hardest with Liam Donegal before an arrest for assaulting a UPW vice president cut his push short.

name: "Poetry in Motion" Percy Monroe

tenures.note: Debuted 17 January 2017 with wife/manager Patricia Monroe at ringside, beating Luscious Jasmine after Patricia yanked the referee off a near-fall. Cost Chad Allen a match against Harrison Daniels III (an old friend of Percy's) by chairing Allen from ringside on 17 January 2017, then lost to John Herdick on 11 April 2017 after a run of bullying the underdog on the mic. Ranked #2 TV Title contender on UPW's own rankings sheet.

caption: "Poetry in Motion" Percy Monroe arrived with his wife Patricia at ringside and spent his short UPW run bullying underdogs before John Herdick beat him.

name: Patricia Monroe

tenures.note: Manager and wife of Percy Monroe, billed as protective "by any means necessary." Pulled a referee off a near-fall to cost Luscious Jasmine his debut match against Percy (17 January 2017) and brawled ringside with Iris Galiver the same night. Clashed with UPW security backstage over locker-room arrangements until old family friend Harrison Daniels III vouched for the couple.

caption: Patricia Monroe managed her husband Percy through UPW's own final months, pulling referees and picking fights with rival managers at ringside.

name: Harrison Daniels III

tenures.note: Debuted 4 October 2016 defeating Tripp Skylark, self-billed "UPW's Redeemer." Entered a UPW Television Championship ladder match on 13 December 2016. Old friend of Percy Monroe and his wife Patricia, vouching for them backstage on 17 January 2017 the same night he beat Chad Allen (with Percy's own interference doing the real work), then shoved Percy away afterward over the tactic. Received a North American Title tournament bye when Malcom Shabazz was arrested (18 February 2017), losing the resulting semifinal to Antonio De Luca. Lost to Tripp Skylark's new, darker persona on 11 April 2017, UPW's own final episode.

caption: Harrison Daniels III debuted a self-styled redeemer, spent a season entangled with an old friend's marriage drama, and closed out UPW's own final broadcast on the losing end of Tripp Skylark's heel turn.

name: Desi Valdez, Jr.

tenures.note: Never appears wrestling in any served show script; known only as a roster listing, a #5-ranked Television Title contender, and a billed opponent (against Luscious Jasmine) on the card previewed for 25 April 2017 — a show the league's own closure two days earlier meant was never held.

caption: Desi Valdez, Jr. survives only as a roster listing and a ranked contender's name — the card that would have shown him in the ring never aired.

name: "Jester" Chad Allen

identity.note: The registry's own jester-chad-allen-rspwf carries the exact same decorated name from the RSPWF Top 200 (2003-04, tagged IGA in 2004), with no fed tag or other detail this UPW wrestler's own record corroborates; recorded distinct per the no-auto-merge rule.

tenures.finisher: The Last Laugh (fireman's-carry death valley driver)
tenures.note: Billed a 20-plus-year veteran and "Wicked Clown"-styled former champion of nearly every organization he's wrestled; debuted 4 October 2016 beating John Herdick behind manager Iris Galiver's repeated interference. Won a title-shot eliminator over "Good" Gordon Gaines (29 December 2016, Galiver interfering again), entered the North American Title tournament (lost to Glenn Chambers, 18 February 2017, reversing Allen's own finisher), and lost the promotion's own last-ever Chad Allen appearance to Caleb Foley (11 April 2017).

caption: "Jester" Chad Allen leaned on manager Iris Galiver's interference through UPW's own life, from his debut win over John Herdick to a North American Title tournament loss to Glenn Chambers.

name: Iris Galiver

tenures.note: Manager/valet of Chad Allen, written as an adult with a child's mind, complete with an imaginary friend ("Mr. Peabody") and a recurring "days of bloodshed" monologue. Interfered behind the referee's back in nearly every Allen match across UPW's run, most consequentially costing Glenn Chambers a clean finish on 18 February 2017 by repeatedly distracting referee Rob Garcia.

caption: Iris Galiver managed "Jester" Chad Allen through UPW's own run with a mind seemingly stuck in childhood, distracting referees behind their backs match after match.

name: Ricky Courage

tenures.role: wrestler — UPW World Tag Team Champion (as part of Soldiers of the Sun)
tenures.note: Rookie member of Soldiers of the Sun, wrestling to honor a wrestler father he never knew ("Stevie" per one on-air reference). Emotional pre-Survival interview framed the Ultimate Rumble and a World Tag Team Title shot as chasing his father's unfinished career. Abandoned mid-match by stablemate Titan Juarez on 29 December 2016 (Juarez's brief defection to the Warriors), reconciled with Juarez on 17 January 2017 after Juarez turned on his new allies. Won UPW's own World Tag Team Championship at Survival (5 March 2017) in a Fatal Four-Way, then was ambushed and laid out with two consecutive "Stomping Ground" finishers by the Dominion on 11 April 2017, moments after signing an autograph for a young disabled fan.

caption: Ricky Courage wrestled to honor the father he never knew, riding Soldiers of the Sun to UPW's own World Tag Team Championship before the Dominion left him broken on the entrance ramp in the promotion's own final broadcast.

name: Titan Juarez

tenures.role: wrestler — UPW World Tag Team Champion (as part of Soldiers of the Sun)
tenures.note: Masked member of Soldiers of the Sun who abandoned his own stablemates mid-match against the Warriors on 29 December 2016, briefly aligning with the Warriors before turning on them by chokeslamming both Dominion members during a title match he ran into on 17 January 2017 and rejoining Soldiers of the Sun. Reconciled fully with Ricky Courage and STRIKER Kato by 18 February 2017, when the Dominion's own interference in a Warriors match drew Juarez back to the ring for a save. Co-held UPW's own World Tag Team Championship after Survival.

caption: Titan Juarez's mid-season defection from Soldiers of the Sun to the Warriors and back was UPW's own longest-running tag-scene storyline, ending in a reconciliation and a World Tag Team Championship.

name: STRIKER Kato

tenures.role: wrestler — UPW World Tag Team Champion (as part of Soldiers of the Sun)
tenures.note: Billed as an Osakan striker and founding member of Soldiers of the Sun alongside Ricky Courage and Titan Juarez. Chaired at ringside by the Warriors' Kel Robertson during a title match on 29 December 2016. Co-held UPW's own World Tag Team Championship after Survival (5 March 2017), retaining against the Down South Connection on UPW's own final broadcast.

caption: STRIKER Kato's speed rounded out Soldiers of the Sun, the trio that carried UPW's own World Tag Team Championship through the promotion's final months.

name: "The Angel" DeAwn Carter

tenures.role: wrestler — UPW World Tag Team Champion (as part of the Warriors)
tenures.note: Half of the Warriors alongside Kel Robertson, managed by Sammy Sharifi. Won UPW's own first World Tag Team Championship from the Hype on the debut show (20 September 2016) in a match Carter and Robertson framed as a stand against the wrestling business's own bigotry. Held the belts until losing them to Soldiers of the Sun, the Dominion, and the O'Malley Brothers in a Survival Fatal Four-Way (5 March 2017).

caption: "The Angel" DeAwn Carter co-held UPW's own first World Tag Team Championship, framing the Warriors' title reign as a stand against bigotry in the business.

name: "The Hound" Kel Robertson

tenures.role: wrestler — UPW World Tag Team Champion (as part of the Warriors)
tenures.note: Half of the Warriors alongside DeAwn Carter, managed by Sammy Sharifi; self-described as "part Native American." Hit the deciding "Justice" piledriver to win the tag titles on UPW's own debut show (20 September 2016). Chaired Soldiers of the Sun's STRIKER Kato at ringside during a title defense (29 December 2016) and abandoned Titan Juarez to a beating rather than help him during a tag match (17 January 2017) shortly before Juarez turned on the Warriors outright.

caption: "The Hound" Kel Robertson's spike piledriver won UPW's own first World Tag Team Championship for the Warriors, a reign he held onto with increasingly ugly ringside tactics.

name: CJ "Mackie" Messer

tenures.note: Half of the Hype alongside "Downtown" Danny Nash, billed an MMA-schooled knockout artist and managed by Syn. Challenged the Warriors for UPW's own vacant, inaugural World Tag Team Championship on the promotion's debut show (20 September 2016), losing two falls to one, then beat the Brothers Grimm's Grimmace with a "Dominator" on 4 October 2016.

caption: CJ "Mackie" Messer's Hype fell just short of UPW's own first World Tag Team Championship on the promotion's debut night.

name: "Downtown" Danny Nash

tenures.note: Half of the Hype alongside CJ "Mackie" Messer, billed a flamboyant showman ("the screenshot king") and managed by Syn. Lost UPW's own inaugural World Tag Team Championship match on the debut show (20 September 2016). Ambushed with chairs by the Dominion on 13 December 2016 in an angle that scrapped a scheduled Hype/O'Malley Brothers match a third time; security pulled him clear of a piledriver on exposed concrete.

caption: "Downtown" Danny Nash's Hype came up just short of UPW's own first World Tag Team Championship, and later took the worst of the Dominion's own arrival as a stable.

name: Syn

tenures.note: Manager of the Hype (CJ Messer and Danny Nash), billed in a Hawaiian shirt with a flask. Ejected from ringside for striking DeAwn Carter during the Hype's own World Tag Team Championship match on UPW's own debut show (20 September 2016).

name: "Adonis" Lance Donovan

tenures.role: wrestler — UPW North American Champion (as part of the Dominion's own run)
tenures.note: Third-generation wrestler billed "making a name for himself across the indies"; joined Antonio De Luca and Tyson Bishop in founding stable the Dominion on 4 October 2016, costing Liam Donegal a match that night. Interfered repeatedly through UPW's run on De Luca's and Bishop's behalf, including De Luca's North American Title tournament win (18 February 2017) and Windham Brody's Television Title win over Brandon Franklin (11 April 2017). Quoted Joseph Chamberlain on empire before the Survival Ultimate Rumble, declaring "the day of the stand-alone wrestlers is gone."

caption: "Adonis" Lance Donovan helped found the Dominion, the stable whose interference underwrote both a North American Championship and a Television Championship change during UPW's own final year.

name: "The American Nightmare" Tyson Bishop

tenures.role: wrestler — UPW North American Champion (as part of the Dominion's own run)
tenures.note: Billed a barrel-chested enforcer who "punished men in Japan"; joined Antonio De Luca and Lance Donovan in founding stable the Dominion on 4 October 2016. Combo finisher with Donovan, "The Stomping Ground" (gutwrench powerbomb into a diving neckbreaker). Referred to consistently as "Tyson Bishop" throughout the corpus except one full episode (13 December 2016), which calls him "Tyler Bishop" instead — carried as an aka rather than corrected, per the museum's verbatim-serving rule.

caption: "The American Nightmare" Tyson Bishop's power rounded out the Dominion, the stable behind both a North American and a Television Championship change in UPW's own final year.

name: Marcus O'Malley

tenures.note: Half of the O'Malley Brothers with Anthony O'Malley, an Irish/Italian-gimmicked tag team whose UPW debut against the Hype was scrapped three separate times by Dominion interference. Handcuffed to a backstage pipe before a six-man tag against the Dominion (29 December 2016), breaking free mid-match to even the numbers; the Dominion piledrove him afterward at ringside. Won UPW's own World Tag Team Championship shot alongside his brother, the Warriors, and Soldiers of the Sun in the Survival Fatal Four-Way (5 March 2017), though the belts went to Soldiers of the Sun.

caption: Marcus O'Malley spent his UPW run on the wrong end of the Dominion's own interference, from a scrapped debut to a handcuffed ambush, before a Survival title shot came up short.

name: Anthony O'Malley

tenures.note: Half of the O'Malley Brothers with Marcus O'Malley. Their scheduled UPW debut against the Hype was scrapped three times running by Dominion interference; backstage, the brothers ambushed Dominion's Bishop and Donovan and had the upper hand until Antonio De Luca turned the tide (13 December 2016). Made the save for a beaten Titan Juarez during a Warriors/Soldiers of the Sun tag match (18 February 2017). Fell short of UPW's own World Tag Team Championship in the Survival Fatal Four-Way (5 March 2017).

caption: Anthony O'Malley's tag run with his brother was defined by a running feud with the Dominion, from three scrapped debuts to a Survival title shot that came up empty.

name: "King of the South" Kenneth Morlock

Lost to Soldiers of the Sun on UPW's own final broadcast (11 April 2017).

caption: "King of the South" Kenneth Morlock's Down South Connection talked a big game about UPW's own tag division and backed it up in their debut win, though it ran out against Soldiers of the Sun on the promotion's final show.

tenures.note: Half of the Down South Connection with Kenneth Morlock, debuting 29 December 2016. Won the team's own in-ring debut against Michael Turner and Isaac "Hooch" Johnson on 17 January 2017. Lost to Soldiers of the Sun on UPW's own final broadcast (11 April 2017).

caption: "The Expert" Matt Allen's Down South Connection won its UPW debut and closed out the promotion's own history on the losing side of a title match.

name: Lenny Masher

name: Doug Trasher

tenures.note: Half of the Columbus Crushers alongside Lenny Masher, jobbing to Soldiers of the Sun in a special-referee tag match worked by a comically biased Sammy Sharifi (13 December 2016). No other appearance found in the held record.

name: "The Phoenix" Adam Lazarus

tenures.role: manager — formerly a UPW World Champion (pre-relaunch, broadcast-attested)
tenures.note: Masked manager of Liam Donegal, billed a former World Champion and rumored-dead ex-reality-TV star; carries a steel-blue cane and, in one segment, a Louisville Slugger. Masked assailant Malcom Shabazz opened Lazarus's head on an exposed turnbuckle (4 October 2016) as an intimidation angle against Donegal. Ejected from ringside for striking Dylan Cardinal during the Fatal Four-Way that crowned UPW's own first post-relaunch World Champion (29 December 2016). Left ringside during a Donegal match (13 December 2016) to protect Donegal's threatened wife and infant son instead.

caption: "The Phoenix" Adam Lazarus managed Liam Donegal through UPW's own opening year, absorbing the worst of the promotion's ugliest angle to protect his client's family.

name: Velvet Sims

tenures.note: Flamboyant, purple-suited manager of Derek Rage throughout UPW's run, present at ringside for Rage's World Heavyweight Championship win over Aaron Lewis at Survival (per the front page's own title report) and his contract-signing face-off ahead of it (18 February 2017). Billed by "Too Cool" Chris Hopper as UPW's own longest-reigning World Champion's own manager going into the Ultimate Rumble.

caption: Velvet Sims managed Derek Rage to UPW's own World Heavyweight Championship, a fixture at ringside through the promotion's final year.

identity.note: The registry's own aka-collision guard reads this manager's own first name as a normalized substring match against WWA's own velvet-wwa; different fed, no other detail connecting the two beyond the shared first name. Recorded distinct per the no-auto-merge rule.

name: Walt Watts

tenures.note: Manager of Brandon Franklin, introduced backstage after Franklin's Television Championship time-limit draw with Felix Sandoval (17 January 2017), vowing to force a rematch. Present for Franklin's own Ultimate Rumble number draw ahead of Survival.

caption: Walt Watts managed Brandon Franklin through the back half of UPW's own run, starting with a vow to avenge a Television Title time-limit draw.

name: "Marvelous" Marco Matters

tenures.note: New signee billed with an ex-military background, prior wrestling in Japan, and a wealthy New York City lifestyle; introduced via a taped vignette (8 November 2016). Lost to Jeff Keenan (29 December 2016), then was squashed by Chase Williams as a message to World Champion Aaron Lewis (17 January 2017), Williams continuing the beating past the bell.

caption: "Marvelous" Marco Matters debuted with a big-money gimmick and an early win, before Chase Williams used him as a message to Aaron Lewis.

name: Derrick "DJ" Jackson

tenures.note: Glenn Chambers's amateur-wrestling protégé, an eighteen-year-old college student wrestling under a false pretense (an "unsanctioned exhibition," to protect his amateur eligibility) that turned into a real beatdown by Dylan Cardinal, who faked a bandaged arm for the whole match before dropping the act. The referee stopped the match rather than let it continue; Chambers arrived too late for the save. Fan-tweeted well wishes during Jackson's hospitalization are referenced on the following two broadcasts, driving Chambers's own feud with Cardinal for the rest of UPW's run. No further in-ring appearance found.

caption: Derrick "DJ" Jackson's lone UPW appearance was a lured-in beatdown by Dylan Cardinal that hospitalized him and fueled Glenn Chambers's feud with Cardinal for the rest of the promotion's life.

name: "Playboy" Ronnie D

Co-host Robert "The Gorilla" Smith separately recalled wrestling him "in NeCW back in the day" on the same broadcast — a further fed, not one the RSPWF placement itself tags, but consistent with the same well-traveled billing.

caption: "Playboy" Ronnie D was announced as UPW's own first 2017 Hall of Fame inductee days before the promotion closed, the induction itself never held.

name: Archibald Smythe

name: Ryan Keys

tenures.note: IXWA developmental wrestler drawing a number for the Survival Ultimate Rumble; self-billed the promotion's own longest-reigning Light Heavyweight Champion, cutting a megaphone-assisted trash-talk promo aimed at the UPW locker room.

caption: Ryan Keys talked up his own IXWA Light Heavyweight reign on his way into UPW's own Ultimate Rumble.

tenures.role: authority-figure — minority owner; wrestler (retired, broadcast-attested)
tenures.note: Named 13 December 2016 as the UPW minority owner who purchased a promotion called GEW (its library, roster and intellectual property, minus its women's division, folding into UPW — Windham Brody's own prior GEW Television Championship among the assets that followed). Thomas Grissom later credits him with originally signing Rick Styles "at a considerable amount of money." Appeared live at the Survival preview desk alongside the regular announce team, discussing the Ultimate Rumble field and UPW's own move away from TTW's old double-elimination Rumble format; recalled sharing old UEW Rumble experiences with Robert Smith.
Undated on the card itself; 2003 is the Wayback capture year, a roster-snapshot date, not an attested tenure span.

tenures.role: authority-figure — Commissioner and later Executive Vice President of Talent Relations

tenures.note: The federation's own rampage0007.html seats him at the Rampage desk beside co-host Robert "The Gorilla" Smith, the same co-host name already carried on this row's own UPW tenure. Smith recalls, "We were one of the top tag teams for the better part of the late nineties," which Hopper does not deny ("Yes it has... Glad to see you be part of this here in Texas"). The federation's own faq.html separately names a real, out-of-character booking-committee member of the same two-part name; that self-introduction is redacted where faq.html is served, since it names a person out of fiction rather than staging this row's own on-screen persona.

caption: "Too Cool" Chris Hopper bought a rival promotion's assets into UPW as its own minority owner and, on the Survival preview desk, traded old-war-story Rumble memories with Robert Smith.

name: Ralph

tenures.role: manager — ringside attendant to Rick Styles; wrestler (one comedy squash)
tenures.note: Pulled from the crowd as a comic prop and "hired" as Rick Styles's own corner man (20 September 2016). Urinated on John Herdick's back on Styles's own order ("Peegate," 8 November 2016), for which Herdick beat Ralph almost instantly in a comedy squash (13 December 2016) after Ralph fainted from fear on contact — his own only in-ring appearance. Added his own weight to help Styles cheat a pinfall over Herdick (29 December 2016). Present at Styles's side for the Survival number draw.

caption: Ralph, plucked from the crowd to be Rick Styles's own corner man, spent his UPW run absorbing the fallout of Styles's own worst schemes — including the one everyone still calls "Peegate."

name: Erin Brokovich

tenures.role: manager — ringside attendant/valet to Rick Styles
tenures.note: Billed a self-described superfan of Rick Styles, introduced by her full name (a parody of the real Erin Brockovich) on UPW's own debut show and thereafter credited only as "Erin." A fixture of Styles's own ringside entourage through the promotion's life, including his own Survival number draw.

caption: Erin Brokovich's superfan devotion to Rick Styles made her a fixture at his side for the whole of UPW's own run.

name: Phil Coulter

tenures.role: authority-figure — CEO
tenures.note: UPW's own CEO, per its FAQ deliberately kept off-camera ("the most successful figureheads are the ones who don't concern themselves with being on TV") and named but never shown across every served episode. Called "Paul Coulter" once, on UPW's own debut broadcast, against "Phil Coulter" everywhere else including the FAQ's own byline — carried as an aka rather than corrected. Robert "The Gorilla" Smith's own on-air outburst ("You tell Coulter and the rest of them to keep me the hell away from him!", 11 April 2017) addresses him by surname alone, consistent with this identification.

caption: Phil Coulter ran UPW as its own deliberately camera-shy CEO, named on nearly every broadcast and shown on none of them.

name: "The Man" Stan Conlon

caption: "The Man" Stan Conlon's dry, old-school play-by-play called every match UPW ever broadcast.

name: Pepper Jackson

tenures.role: commentator — color

caption: Pepper Jackson's brash color commentary, deliberately short on technical wrestling knowledge, ran opposite Stan Conlon on every Showdown UPW aired.

name: Eric Chaney

tenures.role: commentator — studio host

caption: Eric Chaney anchored UPW's own studio desk for the whole of Showdown's run, right through the Survival preview show.

name: Robert "The Gorilla" Smith

tenures.role: commentator — studio co-host; wrestler (retired, broadcast-attested)
tenures.note: UPW's own Showdown studio co-host opposite Eric Chaney, per the FAQ formerly "The Gorilla" of tag team the Crazed Animals. Recalled sharing old UEW Rumble war stories, and wrestling "Too Cool" Chris Hopper in NeCW, on the Survival preview desk (see Hopper's own entry). Had an on-air profanity outburst reacting to Rick Styles's attack on Aaron Lewis (11 April 2017), formally apologizing to the audience the following segment.

caption: Robert "The Gorilla" Smith brought a retired tag-team wrestler's own war stories to UPW's studio desk for the whole of the promotion's run.

name: Dyan Ciccarelli

tenures.role: interviewer — backstage
tenures.note: UPW's own lead backstage interviewer, per the FAQ its own answer to "looks, body, charisma and brains" for interview segments; conducted the great majority of UPW's own backstage promos across the full run. caption: Dyan Ciccarelli conducted nearly every backstage interview UPW ever aired.

name: Thomas Grissom

tenures.role: authority-figure — VP of Talent Relations / road agent
tenures.note: UPW's own VP of Talent Relations, per the FAQ (billed there as "road agent") a 25-year road-agent veteran and former wrestler with an estranged son also in the business. Made and enforced on-air rulings throughout UPW's run: confronting Malcom Shabazz over insubordination (8 November 2016), booking an impromptu no-DQ match on the spot (29 December 2016), naming special referees, and setting stipulations for Survival. Hospitalized on 18 February 2017 in a brawl for which Malcom Shabazz was arrested; sucker-punched by Rick Styles trying to intervene in the arson attack on Aaron Lewis (11 April 2017).

caption: Thomas Grissom's on-air rulings shaped UPW's own storylines from the promotion's first months to its last, at the physical cost of a hospitalization and a sucker punch along the way.

name: Jesse Williams

tenures.role: authority-figure — head trainer
tenures.note: UPW's own head trainer, running the "Sniper's Shot" wrestling school in Pittsburgh per the FAQ, with a promised annual graduating class each June. "Good" Gordon Gaines's own bio card credits him by name as the trainer who developed Gaines's in-ring persona at an earlier promotion (End Zone Wrestling) before recommending him to UPW.

caption: Jesse Williams trained UPW's own talent pipeline through his Pittsburgh wrestling school, developing at least one bio-card wrestler's whole in-ring persona before UPW ever signed him.

name: Steve Blaine

tenures.role: interviewer — backstage / ring announcer for number draws

Called "Thomas Blaine" once by Stan Conlon on the promotion's own final broadcast, against "Steve" everywhere else including his own dialogue tags.

caption: Steve Blaine joined UPW's announce team late in its run and ended up hosting the promotion's biggest number draw and its ugliest post-match interview alike.

tenures.note: Half of the Gentrifiers with Greg Johnson; his card calls him the one who aims his partner.

name: "Studd Muffin" Tiberius Nixon
caption: A denim-clad middle-aged manager who prefers to be called Nixon, "Studd Muffin" Tiberius Nixon walks Damian Payne and Johnny Psychotic to the ring.

tenures.note: Manager of Johnny Psychotic and Damian Payne; his card says he hates the name Tiberius and prefers Nixon.

name: "Bad Karma" RJ Souza
caption: Billed by the announcers as a three-time CWF World Champion, "Bad Karma" RJ Souza entered the 2017 Ultimate Rumble at number seven and was thrown out by Antonio De Luca.

tenures.note: Billed by the announcers as a three-time CWF World Champion; entered the 2017 Ultimate Rumble at number seven and was eliminated by Antonio De Luca.

identity.note: The RSPWF Top 200 of 2004 places an RJ Souza at #192, tagged ECLW; the Rumble bills this wrestler from the CWF and names no ECLW, so nothing joins the two and they are kept apart.

name: "Cowboy" Ken Curtis
caption: Hailed by the announcers as a returning legend, "Cowboy" Ken Curtis entered the 2017 Ultimate Rumble at number twenty-six and lasted until Dylan Cardinal threw him out in seventh place.

tenures.note: Entered the 2017 Ultimate Rumble at number twenty-six to the announcers' surprise as a returning legend, eliminated Malcom Shabazz and Playboy Ronnie D, and finished seventh, thrown out by Dylan Cardinal.

identity.note: The RSPWF polls place a "Cowboy" Ken Curtis at #8 in 1998 (tagged SCRA) and #23 in 2000 (tagged LVPWA), and a Ken Curtis among 1998's Top 100 Brawlers; the Rumble calls this wrestler a legend of earlier years but names none of his federations, so nothing joins them and they are kept apart.
